date.label: Undated Joshua narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: God commissions Joshua as Moses’ successor (Joshua 1:1–9)
East-bank warriors are required to assist the rest of Israel (Joshua 1:12–18)
Rahab hides two spies and extracts a conditional oath (Joshua 2:1–21)
Rahab is characterized as a zonah in Joshua (Joshua 2:1)

connections.note: Joshua 1:5–9 echoes the commissioning already given in Deuteronomy 31:6–8, and does not describe a second succession event.
Deuteronomy 31:23 records the LORD's own charge to Joshua, and Joshua 1:5–9 repeats that commission at the crossing.
The earlier scouting mission in Numbers 13 offers a literary contrast to the mission in Joshua 2, since the personnel and the mission differ.
The Jericho narrative later recounts the fulfilment of the oath made to Rahab in Joshua 2.
Hebrews 11:31 recalls Rahab as an example of faith, a later Christian reception of the Joshua narrative rather than a prophecy.
James 2:25 recalls Rahab as an example of works, a later theological reception of the Joshua narrative rather than a prophecy.
